Generate a factor variable with value labels and an optional variable label

Source: R/misc.R
fkr_factor.Rd

Draws from values (the underlying, often numeric, codes) and returns a factor() over them, optionally relabeled with human-readable labels (the value set) and tagged with a label (a variable-level description), mirroring the "variable label" / "value labels" distinction common in survey/statistical data (e.g. SPSS, Stata, haven).

Usage

fkr_factor(n, values, labels = NULL, label = NULL, prob = NULL)

Arguments

n

Number of values to generate. A single non-negative whole number.

values

A non-empty atomic vector of underlying codes/levels, with no NAs (e.g. c(1, 2) or c("M", "F")).

labels

Optional character vector of display labels, the same length as values and in the same order (e.g. c("Male", "Female") for values = c(1, 2)). If NULL (default), values are used as their own labels, as in a plain factor().

label

Optional single string describing the variable itself (e.g. "Respondent's biological sex"), attached as attr(x, "label") – not to be confused with labels, the per-value display text.

prob

Optional numeric vector of sampling weights, the same length as values. Default NULL draws every value with equal probability.

Value

A factor of length n with levels values (coerced to character, per factor()'s usual behavior) and, if given, an attr(x, "label") variable description. Note that as.integer() on the result gives each value's position in values, not the original code – use levels() or as.character() to recover the original values.

Examples

fkr_factor(5, values = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))
#> [1] Male   Male   Male   Female Male  
#> Levels: Male Female
fkr_factor(5,
  values = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"),
  label = "Respondent's biological sex"
)
#> [1] Female Female Female Female Female
#> attr(,"label")
#> [1] Respondent's biological sex
#> Levels: Male Female
fkr_factor(5, values = c(1, 2, 3), prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1))
#> [1] 1 1 1 1 1
#> Levels: 1 2 3
